messages:
alex: Heads-up — after the kernel-hint rollout this morning I'm seeing a p95 increase on the continuous batcher for small-input workloads. Seems tied to a spike in KV prefetch traffic. Snapshot: https://redwood.internal/perf/trace/2387654321

deploy-bot: Alert — perf-regression observed: continuous-batcher p95 +18% in us-west-2 at 10:34 UTC

maria: I can repro locally with a trace. Batches are forming earlier but microbatch sizes collapse to 1-2 because prefetch reservations are eating the token pool.

sam: Could be token-accounting: prefetch requests currently count against token_budget but often end up not using KV (so cost is over-reserved).

jia: I dug into a profiler — kernel selection is falling back for many microbatches because prefetch threads pin cores and change seq-length distribution. Profiler summary below:

```
profiler:
  kernel_choice: attention_fast (60%) -> fallback_basic (40%)
  avg_sequence_len: 32 -> 64 (mismatch path)
  kv_prefetch_rate: baseline 0.18 req/s -> spike 0.8 req/s
  cpu_pin_time_pct: prefetch threads +12%
```

priyanka: Proposal: split out a small "prefetch token" pool that prefetchers draw from. Those tokens shouldn't reduce admission budget for latency-sensitive requests. Also add a soft-limit so prefetch backpressure happens before user-facing 429s.

alex: I like that. Also: add a probation window for kernel-hint rollouts — keep admit ceiling at 80% for the first 30m and sample ~10% of traffic on the legacy kernel for regression detection.

maria: Config sketch I put together:

```
admission:
  token_budget_per_queue: 1200
  prefetch_pool: 120
  prefetch_soft_limit_pct: 0.6
  probation:
    duration_s: 1800
    admit_ceiling_pct: 0.8
    sample_pct: 0.1
  soft_429:
    enabled: true
    threshold_pct: 0.92
    ramp_seconds: 60
```

sam: Quick question: how do we fold KV cache hits into the budget math? If hits reduce token cost we should apply a kv_hit_factor in the admission calc.

jia: Agreed. We can compute kv_hit_factor = 1 - avg_miss_rate (weighted by model). Current avg miss ~0.25 -> factor ~0.75. We should apply per-model multiplier since smaller models have different hit curves.

priyanka: Also suggest a short "probation token boost" to avoid oscillation after kernel switches — give a tiny temporary boost to instances that just flipped kernels so they aren't immediately evicted.

alex: Action items: maria run A/B with prefetch_pool=80 vs 120 and post 30m p50/p95; sam add kv_hit_factor into admission calc and simulate; priyanka implement soft prefetch limiter + probation token boost; jia collect 1h traces across canaries. Reconvene in 2h.

maria: On it. Dashboard: https://redwood.internal/ops/dashboards/cont-batcher?range=1h — will post run outputs when ready.

deploy-bot: Canary 2/5 in us-west flagged minor error rate bump ~0.1% during the test window.

sam: If errors spike, fallback sampled traffic to legacy kernel automatically. Suggest automated rollback trigger: error_rate > 0.5% sustained for 5m -> rollback.

alex: Good call — tagging @oncall if this affects production beyond canary.

priyanka: One more note — when implementing prefetch_pool, ensure eviction order prefers prefetch reservations with LIFO to reduce long-lived prefetch holds.

maria: Will update the sketch and start the A/B runs now.

sam: I'll instrument the admission sim and share results in this thread.

jia: I'll collect kernel-level traces and attach a flame graph after the 1h window.

alex: Thanks team. We'll keep this thread for the experiment logs and decisions.
